<think>The user asks: "Recommend three books on machine learning suited for an intermediate reader. Each entry: title, author, year, why_recommended."

We need to output a JSON object (valid JSON) containing three entries, each with fields: title, author, year, why_recommended. The user wants only a JSON object, no extra text. The system says "You output ONLY a valid JSON object — no prose, no markdown."

Thus we must produce a JSON object with an array of three book objects.

We need to think about appropriate books for an intermediate ML reader. Should be well-known, likely "Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow" by Aurélien Géron (2nd or 3rd edition, year 2019/2022). "Machine Learning Yearning" is more strategy, but maybe not intermediate. "Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning" by Christopher Bishop (2006) is more advanced. "Deep Learning" by Goodfellow, Bengio, Courville (2016) is advanced but could be intermediate. "Machine Learning: A Probabilistic Perspective" by Kevin Murphy (2012) is advanced. "The Elements of Statistical Learning" by Hastie, Tibshirani, Friedman (2009) is advanced. "Fundamentals of Machine Learning for Predictive Data Analytics" maybe.

Better to choose books that are intermediate: "Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow" (2nd edition, 2019) is intermediate. "Machine Learning with PyTorch and Scikit-Learn" maybe but not needed. "Applied Predictive Modeling" by Max Kuhn and Kjell Johnson (2013) is intermediate. "Machine Learning Engineering" by Andriy Burkov (2020) is also intermediate. "Deep Learning with Python" by François Chollet (2017) is intermediate
